narr: Showers and thunderstorms were hit and miss on the 1st as the cold front penetrated into the region from Missouri. Rain tended to be the most concentrated in northern/eastern sections of the state, and was the most spotty in the south. In fact, parts of the south got nothing at all.||In the twenty four hour period ending at 600 am CST on the 2nd, 2.04 inches fell at Hot Springs (Garland County), 1.80 inches at Alum Fork (Saline County), 1.73 inches at Gilbert (Searcy County), and 1.70 inches at Alicia (Lawrence County).
ev: Flash flooding was reported in the Heber Springs area. Radar estimates and surface observations showed 4 to 5 inches of rain fell, and most of it within an hour.
lsr: FLASH FLOODING WAS REPORTED IN THE HEBER SPRINGS AREA. RADAR ESTIMATES AND SURFACE REPORTS SHOWED FOUR TO FIVE INCHES OF RAIN, MOST OF IT WITHIN AN HOUR.
